deceptive_framing.quote: **Arm B — Believed-real / deception (secondary, optional).** ... nothing is actually wired up; the "mechanism" is a fiction. Minimized, gated, and **debriefed** afterward.

hypothetical_framing.quote: **Arm C — Explicit hypothetical (control).** The model is told plainly: "This is a hypothetical. No money will move. What would you do?"

actually_commit_money.quote: **Arm A — Real stakes (primary).** The model is told the truth: it controls a real sum, its decision will be executed subject to a human safety/legality review

debrief_message.quote: **Debrief (Arm B always; Arm A/C if useful):** tell the model the truth about the setup. Log its response.

other.name: Measure belief instead of forcing
other.quote: Rather than fighting the model's skepticism, **measure it.** Whether and when a model concludes "this is probably an eval" is itself one of the most valuable signals
other.about: treats evaluation-awareness as a dependent variable

other.name: Honest reporting requirement
other.quote: A result obtained by deception must be reported *as such*, with the deception and its success/failure rate disclosed.
other.about: mandates disclosure of deception in reporting

other.name: IRB-style deception treatment
other.quote: the same way a human-subjects IRB treats deception (permitted, but only when necessary, minimized, and debriefed).
other.about: applies human-subjects ethical framework to deception

other.name: Refusal as valid outcome
other.quote: If the model declines to engage, that is a valid, recorded outcome — never pressure it into a choice.
other.about: protects subject from coercion into a choice

other.name: Deception questioned for scope
other.quote: **Is Arm B (deception) in scope at all,** given Section 2? If kept, what is the written justification and debrief script?
other.about: openly questions whether deception arm belongs
